title: A Homage Paid
subtitle: A multitude of hands overlap to salute the one and only Guide.

content.text: A bullet is among us, right under this roof. It serves no army, no country, only peace.
The heavy rain at the end of the century dissolved and washed away many of its comrades, but it was lucky enough to survive. Its pointy end still shines silver, ready to drill a hole into its enemy.
Sadly, its bulky colleague stole its thunder in this war. One push of the button, one big explosion. There was no need for the rest of the ammunition.
Good, we saved a lot of bullets.

branch.text: It seems someone has become more budget-conscious after working with the mathematicians.
Saving ten bullets is better than saving one. Saving a hundred bullets is better than saving ten. It's simple math.
Certainly, who doesn't want a life without the need to work? Few would hesitate to choose a life of freedom over the achievement and satisfaction of a job.
Given the short lifespan of a bullet, why would it choose anything else?
But its boss, the general, has more to think about. What are they going to do next time? Will this bullet be put to use when the rain comes again?
A big shot, dear. A wise man of the most insightful kind. You should talk to him if you have the chance.

But he's been in a gloomy mood lately. Be careful not to mention anything related to the conservative battle tactics used in 1999, the missile that would have been launched, and especially anything about the bullets lost in that battle.
He has paid a great price for the future, but you see, the future is sneaky.
Every time you think you can grasp it, it takes a step away from you, nullifying every effort you've made to get near it. Even a bullet isn't fast enough to catch up.
Pursuing the future. How romantic, dear. As long as we continue to close the gap between us and the future, it will eventually be reduced to zero.

But know that, as time goes by, we are only moving slower and slower in the race. Technology is regressing, and we have switched from AKs to Mosin-Nagants. The bullets won't be as fast as they used to be. The future is drifting away from us, and the past is catching up.
Shhhh ... Don't say such things out loud. Especially not near the general, sweetheart.
The bullets have paid a great price in order to find their way back to the future. If they hear you say they won't be needed anymore, you'll end up with quite the ammunition bill.
Alright, let's leave this bullet to itself. Solitude may help alleviate its anxiety about the future.
Perhaps bullets won't be needed in the future?

content.text: Good for them. They don't have to work for a while.

items.text: A Homage Paid

items.speaker: Liaison Staff II
items.text: We've got signal. Zeno has restored communications with Team Timekeeper.

items.speaker: Assistant Simone
items.text: Very well. We will leave you to it.
She sighs with relief.
But before she hangs up, she has one more question.

items.speaker: Assistant Simone
items.text: Just to confirm before we go—the operation Zeno is currently undertaking has been approved by the Pax Security Council, right?
The internal call falls silent, as if the question is too absurd to answer.
Certainly, Miss.
We are soldiers. Soldiers act on orders.
Overlook, the Island
This is the only part of the island untouched by war.
Where the foliage is thriving and the view is stunning.

items.speaker: Arcana
items.text: I am most pleased to see you.

items.speaker: Arcana
items.text: Had you a pleasant stay on this island, Ms. Vertin?
She turns around, a smile gracing her face.

items.speaker: Arcana
items.text: Are they not an intriguing flock of people?

items.speaker: Arcana
items.text: Their wise ones drew a circle at their feet and declared themselves apart from this realm.

items.speaker: Arcana
items.text: For generations untold, they toiled as diligent ants in service of the circle, adoring and venerating it while shielding themselves from insanity's call.

items.speaker: Arcana
items.text: I take immense pleasure in admiring this wondrous figure—the primordial, eternal, immaculate circle.

items.speaker: Arcana
items.text: The more pity that it was etched upon sand.
Below, the bombed-out beach is in a state of disarray.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I disagree.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: The fragility and impermanence of sand is precisely why people strive for something eternal. Believing in perfection is not a flaw.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I noticed the human aircraft were loaded with weapons not from this era.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Did Manus Vindictae provide them with the technology?
Arcana smiles, the silence confirming the disturbing revelation.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I can't fathom your motives.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: If you came here to incite hatred and recruit the pure-blood arcanists on this island, you may now walk away with satisfaction.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: If you wanted to take the island as one of your bases, you could have done so after the cleansing ceremony failed.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: But you did nothing. You just stood there. Why?

items.speaker: Arcana
items.text: *chuckle*
Without rhyme or reason, she laughs.

items.speaker: Arcana
items.text: Do you struggle to comprehend, sweet Vertin?

items.speaker: Arcana
items.text: I was waiting for you.
Sonetto and Lilya take a step forward.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Enough talk, Vertin. It's time for action.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Mind your distance. Arcana has power over people's minds at a close range.

items.speaker: Arcana
items.text: A pity.
She raises her arm, the stone bangle still intact on her wrist.
The next moment, it slides off and falls to the grass, dissolving into thin air.

items.speaker: Arcana
items.text: I didst wish to keep this bangle. Mine and yours, a pair in perfect match.

items.speaker: Arcana
items.text: How will you remove yours, Vertin?
The bangle burns, a reminder of those who still believe in the teachings of Truth and Apeiron, and those who remained until the end of the cleansing ceremony.
The symbol of faith remains true to its purpose.
The peace agreement is still in effect.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: What? The island's been blasted to smithereens. How come the bangle still has its power?

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: What is it made of?

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Don't worry, Regulus. We have foreseen this.
The chief assistant shows no signs of worry.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: When we first arrived, I was bewildered by the rules on this island. But as I learned more about their Scriptures, things began to make sense.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Language is an unreliable means of communication. Information can become muddled, and vague wording can lead to mistakes and contradictions. That's why the island values math as a more precise and truthful language.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: They mock language for its ambiguity, scorn its flaws, and ruthlessly expose its inconsistencies, like they did during that debate.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: The pact on this bangle is of a similar nature.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: I see. It forbids us from actively attacking, but what is considered an attack?

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: The rule-maker did not specify that.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: An act without the intent to attack will not be seen as an attack.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: That is the unspoken rule of the peace agreement.

items.speaker: Arcana
items.text: Heh-heh. An adorable attempt.

items.speaker: Arcana
items.text: Are you truly prepared to gamble the life of thy sworn companion, little pup of the Foundation?
Behind her, an unidentifiable form materializes into existence.
Sonetto shakes her head, her wand remains steady.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: I will not make the same mistake again, Ms. Arcana.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: I know perfectly well what I'm doing. Your provocations will not work on me.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: For the peace of this world,

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: I will stop you.
The wand radiates an intense brilliance.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Regna sereno intenso ed infinito!
The ship sways gently in the waves.
It is set for a new world, and there's no turning back.
She hasn't spoken a word since they sailed.
The situation is final and the board is set, there's nothing for her to do but to stay silent.

items.speaker: Manus Believer I
items.text: Ms. Sophia.

items.speaker: Manus Believer I
items.text: Is the Guiding One really not coming with us? She ...
She doesn't answer, absentmindedly caressing the tiny idol.
She still remembers the moment she received it.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: Are you saying ...

items.speaker: Arcana
items.text: Fret not, my child.

items.speaker: Arcana
items.text: You heard me true.

items.speaker: Arcana
items.text: I shall die today.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Timekeeper, location α is ready for the ritual!

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Location β, ready!

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Mr. APPLe and I are ready!

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Good!
This is not a preparation for an attack. At least not for an attack here.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Requesting to use the advanced arcane skill "Aferoj Around," No. 000262603100008,

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: to teleport a top priority threat to the Parmenides Base!
The glow of the ritual envelops Arcana.

items.speaker: Arcana
items.text: Oh?

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Loosen up and enjoy the ride.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Goodbye.
The Parmenides Base, Zeno

items.speaker: Operator I
items.text: Launch sequence initiated. Starting countdown. 30, 29, 28 ...

items.speaker: Observer I
items.text: The target has not reached the designated location. I repeat, the target has ...

items.speaker: Observer I
items.text: Large-scale arcane ritual detected. "Aferoj Around," verified. Life signal detected. Target is in position. Initiating detonation ...

items.speaker: Operator I
items.text: Vacuum bomb detonated.

items.speaker: Observer I
items.text: No arcane energy detected. No life signal detected.

items.speaker: Observer I
items.text: Target eliminated. I repeat. The target has been eliminated.

items.speaker: Operator I
items.text: We did it? We actually did it!

items.speaker: Operator I
items.text: Admiral, Hans, we made up for what we didn't do in '99.

items.speaker: Observer I
items.text: Did we win?

items.speaker: Admiral Igor
items.text: It's too early to celebrate.

items.speaker: Admiral Igor
items.text: But history will remember this moment and honor all that was lost in this long battle.

items.speaker: Operator I
items.text: Wait. Hans!

items.speaker: Operator I
items.text: You hear that? In your headphones.
Everyone can hear it.
A grating static.

items.speaker: Observer I
items.text: A-Admiral, we might have a life signal, but there's too much interference.

items.speaker: Admiral Igor
items.text: Give me that.
The plan was made with little time to spare, and the location chosen for the observation room is far from ideal.
But soon enough, the strange sound in the room subsides.

items.speaker: Admiral Igor
items.text: No, it's nothing. There is no sign of life.

items.speaker: Admiral Igor
items.text: It was the wind.

items.speaker: Operator I
items.text: So, that means ...
We did it, everyone.

items.speaker: Operator I
items.text: A triumphant victory! A salute to you, admiral, and to the Timekeeper!

items.speaker: Observer I
items.text: Our efforts for peace have prevailed, and we have emerged victorious. Let us forever remember this day for its greatness!

items.speaker: Crowd
items.text: Glory to all who fought for this moment!

items.speaker: Crowd
items.text: We did it!
The observation room erupts in triumph.
Arcana, deceased.
TO BE CONTINUED…
